algorithm: Bemis-Murcko scaffolds (RDKit MurckoScaffoldSmiles, includeChirality=False) as indivisible groups; acyclic rows (empty scaffold) form per-molecule singleton groups; sorted group keys permuted by numpy.random.default_rng(split_seed); greedy fill with train<=0.8*N, train+valid<=0.9*N; row ids sorted ascending inside each split

grouping_policy.empty_scaffold: group key "__ACYCLIC__" + SMILES (one group per distinct acyclic molecule)
grouping_policy.rationale: 317/1128 ESOL molecules are acyclic, so a single empty-scaffold group would swallow an entire split (the strict variant leaves Test empty and is recorded below); a per-row singleton key instead lets the 5 duplicated ESOL SMILES straddle splits, so identical acyclic SMILES are kept together

strict_empty_scaffold_alternative.policy: strict: every molecule with the empty Bemis--Murcko scaffold shares group ""
strict_empty_scaffold_alternative.rejected_because: the empty-scaffold block (317 rows) is placed into Validation and Test receives 0 molecules, so no one-shot evaluation would be possible
